q: What goes into the CBAM figure for high-carbon ferrochrome from Inner Mongolia?
title: Inner Mongolia ferrochrome CBAM figure
short: Direct emissions only: carbon from coke and other reductants, electrode paste and any fuel, worked out by mass balance. Ferro-chromium under CN 7202 4 is covered, but the large electricity use of the furnaces is not counted, even where it comes from coal.
audience: Ferrochrome smelters in Inner Mongolia and their EU stainless steel customers

ul: Carbon in coke, semi-coke and coal charged to the furnace, less carbon leaving in the alloy and slag.
Fuel used for drying or preheating ore.

p: Electricity is an indirect emission, and for iron and steel goods, which include ferro-alloys, only direct emissions are charged. It still belongs in any product footprint a buyer asks for.

ul: Reductant purchases with carbon content from lab tests.
Alloy output and its carbon content.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and production documents into dated, fingerprinted installation records, the starting point for the actual emissions an EU importer asks for.

sources.label: IPCC 2006 Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
